fault.name: poison-message
fault.title: The ledger stops booking: a poison message
fault.cause: a deploy of the ledger consumer that retries unreadable messages forever (BAD_EVENTS=retry), then one unreadable event from the provider (a payment.updated with its amount as a decimal string): the ledger consumer is stuck on it, and books nothing behind it
expected_symptoms: the ledger's lag climbs on every partition: one consumer reads all three, and it is stuck on that one message (head-of-line blocking); the payment confirmer keeps up
the ledger's retries climb, with 'could not book; will retry the same message' errors for one offset
the confirmer dead-letters the same event as unreadable; the ledger never does
the ledger consumer turns unhealthy: its heartbeat stops while it retries
the money check cannot settle (exit 2); without waiting, the events behind the poison look lost
fault.remedy: roll the ledger consumer back to dead-lettering: the poison goes to the dead-letter topic, the backlog drains, and the money check passes again

diagnosis.hypothesis: Provider event evt_000260 (provider-events partition 1, offset 113) has an invalid amount: 'amount must be positive integer cents'. The webhook-receiver accepted and queued it at about 02:35:33. ledger-consumer had been redeployed at 02:35:31 with BAD_EVENTS=retry. With that setting it retries the same message forever, backing off up to 15s, and never commits past it. While it waits, it stops processing every partition: the posted rate fell to 0 by about 02:36:34. So the ledger group's lag grows on all three partitions as new events arrive (0, then 91, then 305), which fires ConsumerLagHigh. payment-confirmer runs with BAD_EVENTS=dead_letter. It dead-lettered the same message and keeps up. Still open: why the provider sent a non-positive or non-integer amount, and whether the earlier ledger configuration also used retry.

evidence.shows: The ledger group's lag was 0 at 02:35:08, 91 at 02:36:08 and 305 at 02:37:08, so the alert is real and the lag is growing.
ledger-consumer was redeployed at 02:35:31 with LEDGER_HANDLER=idempotent and BAD_EVENTS=retry. payment-confirmer uses BAD_EVENTS=dead_letter.
ledger-consumer logs 'could not book; will retry the same message' for provider-events/1@113, attempts 3 to 11, error 'amount must be positive integer cents'.
payment-confirmer dead-lettered the same message, provider-events/1@113, with the same amount error.
The trace identifies the message as event evt_000260. The receiver queued it with HTTP 200. The ledger span outcome is will_retry 13 or more times over 105s; the confirmer outcome is dead_lettered.
The lag is spread over all partitions (131, 138, 127), so the whole ledger consumer is blocked, not only partition 1.
The ledger posted and already_processed rates fell to 0 by 02:36:34. payment-confirmer kept processing at about 3 events/s.

proposed_fix.summary: 1. Redeploy ledger-consumer with BAD_EVENTS=dead_letter, as payment-confirmer has. It will then dead-letter evt_000260 and drain the backlog; the idempotent handler makes reprocessing safe. 2. Inspect evt_000260 on the dead-letter queue and in the provider's records. 3. Book or confirm it by hand (data repair) once the correct amount is known. 4. Run money_check afterwards. 5. As a follow-up, consider validating amounts in webhook-receiver.

diagnosis.blast_radius: Only ledger-consumer changes. evt_000260 will be absent from the ledger until it is repaired by hand, so money_check will report it as unposted. Draining about 300 events causes a short burst of load on Postgres. If other malformed events exist, they will also be dead-lettered rather than block the consumer.
diagnosis.rollback_plan: Redeploy ledger-consumer with its previous settings (BAD_EVENTS=retry, same image sha256:a145222baa11). Its committed offsets are kept, so nothing is lost. Any dead-lettered events can be replayed from the dead-letter queue once they are fixed.
